subtitle: From royal silence to a hunter’s scar and a world’s gaze

panels.shot: epic wide of the Waghora gorge with dark cave mouths and a faint silhouette of a lone British officer on a distant ledge
panels.action: The sheer basalt walls of the Waghora gorge curve around a hidden horseshoe of caves, mist curling at dawn as a tiny figure stands on the rim, looking down toward Ajanta’s shadowed entrances.

dialogue.text: Centuries after Ajanta’s royal chants fell silent, a British hunter named John Smith scratched his name over a Bodhisattva’s face—and changed how the world would see these caves forever.

i18n.hi: सदियों बाद, जब अजन्ता की राज-प्रार्थनाएँ थम गईं, ब्रिटिश शिकारी जॉन स्मिथ ने एक बोधिसत्व के चेहरे पर अपना नाम खरोंच दिया—और दुनिया की नज़र हमेशा के लिए बदल दी।

panels.shot: slow push-in from high-angle view of the gorge to the dark cave mouths half hidden by forest
panels.action: Dense forest spills over the lip of the Waghora gorge, roots clutching stone as the river gleams below; along the curve, rock-cut cave facades emerge from shadow, weathered yet solemn.

dialogue.text: When Vakataka patronage faded in the 6th century, Ajanta’s halls grew quiet. The gorge kept its secrets, but the caves never truly vanished.

i18n.hi: छठी सदी में वाकाटकाओं की सरपरस्ती ढली तो अजन्ता के सभागार सुनसान हो गए। घाटी ने राज़ छुपाए, पर गुफाएँ कभी सच में गायब नहीं हुईं।

panels.shot: interior wide of a dim Ajanta vihara centuries later, with a few monks and lay visitors under smoke-darkened paintings
panels.action: Inside a pillared hall, faint murals glow in the half-light as a small group of monks sit in meditation; a couple of local visitors stand respectfully near a carved Buddha, oil lamps flickering.

dialogue.text: Long after kings stopped sending artists and gold, monks still came, villagers still knew the path, and prayers rose beneath peeling paint and cracked stone.

i18n.hi: जब राजाओं ने कलाकार और सोना भेजना छोड़ा, तब भी भिक्षु आते रहे, गाँव वाले रास्ता जानते रहे, और उखड़ती रंगत व टूटी चट्टानों के नीचे प्रार्थनाएँ उठती रहीं।

panels.shot: close-up of a palm-leaf manuscript next to a small travel party moving through rocky Deccan landscape
panels.action: A stylized image shows robed travelers crossing a rocky plateau in the distance, while in the foreground a scribe’s hand hovers over a palm leaf etched with neat Sanskrit lines.

dialogue.text: Texts hint at these caves. Xuanzang in the 7th century, Abu’l-Fazl in the Ain-i-Akbari centuries later—scholars cautiously trace their words to Ajanta’s cliffs.

i18n.hi: ग्रंथों में इन गुफाओं के हल्के सुराग हैं। सातवीं सदी में श्वेनज़ांग, सदियों बाद आईन-ए-अकबरी में अबुल फ़ज़्ल—विद्वान इनके शब्दों को अजन्ता की चट्टानों से जोड़ते हैं।

panels.shot: wide shot of Mughal-era entourage passing far from the gorge, with the distant cliff barely visible
panels.action: A Mughal hunting party rides across a distant ridge, pennants snapping in the wind; far below, barely noticeable, the curve of the Ajanta cliff cuts across the landscape, cloaked in haze.

dialogue.text: Empires rose around Ajanta—the Chalukyas, Rashtrakutas, the Delhi sultans, the Mughals—but its painted Buddhas watched from the shadows, mentioned, perhaps, yet largely untouched.

i18n.hi: अजन्ता के आस-पास साम्राज्य उठे—चालुक्य, राष्ट्रकूट, दिल्ली सल्तनत, मुगल—but रंगे हुए बुद्ध छाया में देखते रहे, शायद ज़िक्र हुआ, पर ज़्यादातर अछूते रहे।

panels.shot: intimate village scene near the gorge, medium shot of locals pointing toward the hidden cliff
panels.action: In a small Deccan hamlet, elders sit beneath a tree while a younger man points toward the distant gorge; behind them, women carry bundles along a path that twists toward the unseen caves.

dialogue.text: For nearby villages, the caves were never a mystery. Paths, stories, names passed from mouth to ear, while official maps ignored the gorge’s carved sanctuaries.

i18n.hi: पास के गाँवों के लिए ये गुफाएँ कभी रहस्य नहीं थीं। रास्ते, किस्से, नाम जुबान से कान तक चलते रहे, जबकि सरकारी नक्शों ने घाटी के तराशे मंदिरों को अनदेखा किया।

panels.shot: dynamic mid-shot of John Smith in uniform on horseback, hunting party behind him moving through dense forest
panels.action: Captain John Smith rides in British cavalry uniform, rifle slung over his shoulder, pushing through thorny undergrowth with a small hunting party, the soundless gorge ahead.

dialogue.text: On 28 April 1819, Captain John Smith of the 28th Cavalry rode into this forest on a tiger hunt, following local guides toward steep, unfamiliar cliffs.

i18n.hi: 28 अप्रैल 1819 को 28वीं कैवेलरी के कप्तान जॉन स्मिथ बाघ के शिकार पर इस जंगल में घुड़े, स्थानीय राह दिखाने वालों के पीछे-पीछे ऊँची, अनजानी चट्टानों की ओर।

panels.shot: low-angle shot from inside the gorge as Smith appears at the rim, peering down toward Cave 10
panels.action: From the floor of the gorge, the camera looks up as John Smith stands on the rim, framed against the sky, shading his eyes as he peers down at a faint, horseshoe-shaped line of cave facades.

dialogue.speaker: john_smith
dialogue.text: What are those cut into the rock?

i18n.hi: ये पत्थर में काटे हुए क्या हैं?

panels.shot: tense wide shot of Smith and a guide descending a precarious path toward the dark entrance of Cave 10
panels.action: John Smith grips a rough rope ladder, descending carefully along the cliff face toward a yawning black entrance; below, a local guide steadies the line, the river glinting in the background.

dialogue.text: Led by men who already knew these hollows, Smith climbed down toward Cave 10—a rock-cut chaitya hall that had watched fourteen centuries pass.

i18n.hi: पहले से इन खोहों को जानने वाले लोगों की राहनुमाई में स्मिथ गुफा 10 तक उतरा—एक चट्टान काटी चैत्यशाला, जो चौदह सदियाँ देख चुकी थी।

panels.shot: wide interior of Cave 10 as Smith steps in, silhouetted against light, the great chaitya arch and stupa ahead
panels.action: John Smith stands at the threshold of Cave 10, his silhouette framed by the bright doorway; ahead, ribs of stone curve toward a stupa, murals faintly visible on the walls and pillars.

dialogue.text: He stepped into a 2nd–5th century chaitya once filled with chanting. Now only the echo of boots on stone broke the long silence.

i18n.hi: वह दूसरी–पाँचवीं सदी की उस चैत्यशाला में कदम रखता है, जहाँ कभी जाप भरा रहता था। अब बस पत्थर पर जूतों की गूँज ने लंबी ख़ामोशी तोड़ी।

panels.shot: medium close-up of a painted Bodhisattva figure on the wall, with Smith’s hand and knife poised near the surface
panels.action: A serene painted Bodhisattva gazes outward from the wall, colors dimmed by age; beside the face, John Smith’s gloved hand presses a knife point to the plaster, ready to scratch.

dialogue.text: Above one Bodhisattva, he carved a mark of his own presence: ‘John Smith, 28 Cavalry, 28 April 1819,’ cutting through the ancient paint.

i18n.hi: एक बोधिसत्व के ऊपर उसने अपने होने का निशान उकेरा: ‘जॉन स्मिथ, 28 कैवेलरी, 28 अप्रैल 1819’, सदियों पुराने रंग पर कट लगाते हुए।

panels.shot: tight close-up on the incised graffito over the painting, with Smith’s face in soft focus behind it
panels.action: The camera focuses on the rough letters gouged into the wall, crossing the haloed figure beneath; behind them, John Smith’s face is blurred, thoughtful yet unaware of the damage.

dialogue.text: The inscription scarred the image, a small but lasting wound. Yet that same act fixed a date and a name that would anchor Ajanta’s modern story.

i18n.hi: उस लिखाई ने चित्र को चीर दिया, छोटा पर टिकाऊ ज़ख्म। पर उसी हरकत ने तारीख और नाम तय कर दिए, जो अजन्ता की आधुनिक कहानी का सहारा बने।

panels.shot: wide shot of Smith leaving the cave, hunting party and local villagers gathered outside, gorge stretching beyond
panels.action: John Smith emerges into daylight, talking with fellow officers and local villagers at the cave mouth, the curve of the gorge and other cave entrances visible behind them.

dialogue.text: Reports followed his visit. British officers and surveyors brought Ajanta into colonial records, calling it a ‘discovery’ though local memory had never let it slip away.

i18n.hi: उसके बाद रिपोर्टें आईं। ब्रिटिश अफ़सर और सर्वेयर अजन्ता को उपनिवेशी रेकॉर्ड में ले आए, इसे ‘खोज’ कहा, जबकि स्थानीय याद ने इसे कभी खोने ही नहीं दिया था।

panels.shot: tabletop shot of early 19th-century sketches and notes of Ajanta spread out under lamplight
panels.action: Under a flickering lamp, careful sketches of cave facades and interior pillars lie beside notebooks filled with English descriptions, rulers and compasses resting nearby.

dialogue.text: As the 19th century moved on, colonial societies sent artists and scholars; Ajanta’s pillars, arches, and faded stories appeared in sketches and printed reports in distant cities.

i18n.hi: उन्नीसवीं सदी बढ़ती गई तो औपनिवेशिक सोसायटियों ने कलाकार और विद्वान भेजे; अजन्ता के स्तंभ, मेहराबें और फीकी कहानियाँ दूर शहरों की रेखाचित्रों और छपी रिपोर्टों में दिखने लगीं।

panels.shot: medium shot of the Nizam’s officials and British scholars in front of a cave entrance, indicating joint concern
panels.action: Officials in Hyderabadi dress stand beside British scholars at a cave doorway, gesturing at cracked pillars and flaking murals, scrolls and measuring chains in their hands.

dialogue.text: Under the Nizam of Hyderabad, Ajanta drew regional attention too. Later, the Archaeological Survey of India stepped in, balancing documentation with early conservation that sometimes harmed what it sought to save.

i18n.hi: हैदराबाद के निज़ाम के दौर में अजन्ता ने इलाकाई ध्यान भी खींचा। बाद में भारतीय पुरातत्व सर्वेक्षण आया, रेकॉर्ड रखने के साथ शुरुआती संरक्षण को साधते हुए, जो कभी-कभी बचाने की चीज़ को ही चोट पहुँचा गया।

panels.shot: mid-shot of G. Yazdani examining a mural with notes in hand, conservators working around
panels.action: G. Yazdani stands before a wall painting, notebook open, while conservators on scaffolds gently work near the surface, the dim hall lit by temporary lamps.

dialogue.text: In the early 20th century, researchers like Ghulam Yazdani studied and photographed Ajanta, preserving its details on paper even as some interventions altered the fragile surfaces.

i18n.hi: बीसवीं सदी के शुरुआती सालों में ग़ुलाम यज़दानी जैसे शोधकर्ताओं ने अजन्ता का अध्ययन और फ़ोटोग्राफ़ी की, बारीकियाँ काग़ज़ पर बचाईं, भले कुछ कामों ने नाज़ुक सतहों को बदल दिया।

panels.shot: scholarly montage: books by Cohen and Mitter on a desk, with a photo of Ajanta behind
panels.action: Modern academic books lie open on a desk—titles by Richard S. Cohen and Partha Mitter—behind them a black-and-white photograph of Ajanta’s caves pinned to the wall.

dialogue.text: Later scholars traced Ajanta’s post-Vakataka life—a place of intermittent worship, local familiarity, colonial fascination, and shifting views on Indian art and Buddhism.

i18n.hi: बाद के विद्वानों ने अजन्ता के वाकाटकाओं के बाद के जीवन को टटोला—कभी-कभार पूजा की जगह, स्थानीयों की जानी-पहचानी, औपनिवेशिक दिलचस्पी, और भारतीय कला व बौद्धधर्म पर बदलती नज़रें।

panels.shot: epic aerial shot of Ajanta in the late 20th century, with visitors on the path and a subtle UNESCO emblem inset as architecture
panels.action: From high above, the horseshoe cliff of Ajanta appears with neat pathways and small groups of visitors; a modest modern signboard stands near the entrance complex, echoing global recognition.

dialogue.text: In 1983, Ajanta joined the UNESCO World Heritage list. The gorge that once held near-silence now welcomed visitors from around the world.

i18n.hi: 1983 में अजन्ता यूनेस्को विश्व विरासत सूची में शामिल हुआ। जो घाट कभी लगभग ख़ामोश था, अब दुनिया भर से आए मेहमानों का स्वागत करता है।

panels.shot: quiet interior wide of Cave 10 today, tourists in silhouette, Bodhisattva with Smith’s graffito visible
panels.action: Modern visitors stand softly in Cave 10, gazing at the ancient Bodhisattva; above the painted face, the old incised words ‘John Smith, 28 Cavalry’ remain, shallow cuts across the halo.

dialogue.text: Ajanta’s afterlife holds both care and scars—from monks and villagers to officers and scholars. Remembering them all keeps the caves alive without erasing those who never forgot them.

i18n.hi: अजन्ता का बाद का जीवन देखभाल और ज़ख्म दोनों से भरा है—भिक्षुओं और गाँव वालों से लेकर अफ़सरों और विद्वानों तक। सबको याद रखना गुफाओं को ज़िंदा रखता है, बिना उन लोगों को मिटाए जिन्होंने इन्हें कभी भूला ही नहीं।

subtitle_i18n.en: From royal silence to a hunter’s scar and a world’s gaze
subtitle_i18n.hi: राजसी ख़ामोशी से शिकारी के निशान तक, दुनिया की नज़र तक
